venue.name: Mount Cain Alpine Park
venue.description: Mount Cain is a ski hill in the mountains above Highway 19 on northern Vancouver Island, operated by the not for profit Mount Cain Alpine Park Society. It has two T-bars and one beginner's handle tow giving access to 21 runs, with a fifth of the terrain rated beginner. The hill opens in early December, snow permitting, and closes in early April, and the lifts run Saturday, Sunday and select Mondays from 9:30am to 3:30pm plus mid week days over the Christmas and spring school breaks. The last 16km to the parking lot is a gravel road that takes about half an hour, and the site says carrying chains is mandatory.

facility_notes.washrooms: Properly dispose of all waste water in one of the outhouses.
facility_notes.lunch_space: Cain Cafe: Friday ~8pm-11pm, Saturday and Sunday 7:30am-11pm (last call, food: 9pm, drinks 10:30pm)
facility_notes.bus_parking: From the Highway 19 turnoff to the Mt Cain parking lot is 16km on a gravel road; about 30 minutes by vehicle. Tow-behind trailers are strongly discouraged.

venue.nearby_park: Schoen Lake Provincial Park has lakeside hiking trails as well as a rough alpine route that leads to Mount Schoen's wildflower meadows.
restrictions: CARRYING CHAINS IS MANDATORY! You must have chains that fit your vehicle, chains that you know how to use, chains that you intend to use!
Chains may be required for going both up and down the access road. Vehicles without chains will be denied access.
Actually putting tire-chains ON is often REQUIRED FOR ALL VEHICLES, including 4x4's with good snow tires.
DO NOT use your phone for instructions, Google Maps, iMaps, etc. will have you turn off the highway too soon.
Children 12 years and under are free to ride the lifts but must have a valid lift pass and have the waiver signed by a guardian.
Tickets are not for sale online.
Dogs must be on a leash at all times. Dogs are not allowed on the ski hill.
When we are closed the road is not maintained and folks are reminded not to trespass on the ski hill.
Please remember there are no services provided by mount cain during mid week days.
venue.hours_notes: Lifts: Saturday, Sunday and select Mondays, 9:30am to 3:30pm, with mid week days over the Christmas and spring breaks. Ticket booth: Friday 7pm to 9pm, Saturday 8:30am to 2pm, Sunday 9am to 2pm. Ski shop: 9am to 4pm on ski hill operational days. Cain Cafe: Friday about 8pm to 11pm, Saturday and Sunday 7:30am to 11pm. Tickets are not for sale online; after 1:30pm and on Mondays lift tickets can be bought at the ski shop.
venue.seasonal_notes: Mount Cain opens in early December (snow permitting) and closes early April, conditions permitting. It is open Saturday, Sunday, select Mondays and during SD85's school winter and spring break. The published operational schedule has opening weekend on December 5 and 6, 2026, a run of Mondays it calls Magic Monday when only the lower mountain runs, mid week opening over spring break from March 13 to 22, 2027, and closing day on April 10, 2027.

programs.name: School or group ski day
programs.description: Mount Cain takes group and school bookings by email. The tickets page says to contact Barb at bcolbourne@mountcain.com, and no group or school rate is published anywhere on the site. The events calendar has listed school group days on Mondays through January, February and March, and the rentals page says the three day rates cover Saturday, Sunday and School Group Mondays when only the lower lifts are operating. Children 12 and under ride the lifts free but still need a valid pass and a waiver signed by a guardian. Youth 13 to 18 pay $38 for a day pass and adults $74 as non members or $64 as members, and none of those figures include GST.
programs.what_children_do: Ride the beginner handle tow or a T-bar and ski or snowboard the 21 runs, a fifth of which are rated beginner. On the Mondays set aside for school groups only the lower lifts run, so the whole day stays on the lower mountain. Snowshoeing around the meadows and forest is the other option, with snowshoes rented from the ski shop.
programs.our_note: Getting there is the hard part. The last 16km off Highway 19 is gravel and takes about half an hour, chains are mandatory for every vehicle including four wheel drives, and the site warns that phone directions send you off the highway too soon. Lifts only run Saturday, Sunday and select Mondays, and school groups are slotted onto those Mondays, so pick a date with Barb early. No group price is published and tickets cannot be bought online, so settle both when you book.
programs.practical_summary: Children 12 and under ride the lifts free and rental helmets are included, but no price for a group is published. There is no street address, the last stretch of road is gravel with chains required, and washrooms, an indoor lunch space and bus parking are not described anywhere, so it is worth a call before you book.
programs.extra_fees_note: Rentals are extra. A full day ski or snowboard bundle is $17 for 12 and under, $26 for youth 13 to 18 and $38 for adults. Helmets are free. Equipment returned after 4:00pm is charged an extra $10. Prices do not include taxes.
programs.evidence: For group or school bookings, please contact Barb via bcolbourne@mountcain.com

programs.name: Learn to Ski / Snowboard Package
programs.description: A beginner package that includes a handle tow ticket, rentals and a one hour lesson. The lessons page and the tickets page give two different prices for it, $48 per person on one and $47.25 plus tax on the other. The site says prices do not include tax.
programs.what_children_do: Put on rented skis or a snowboard, spend an hour with an instructor, and ride the beginner handle tow on the ticket the package includes.
programs.our_note: This is the one to ask about for a group that has never skied, because it rolls the gear, the lesson and the beginner tow into one booking. Two of their pages price it differently, so confirm the figure when you book. Lessons are arranged through the ski shop by email.
programs.practical_summary: The package covers gear, a lesson and the beginner tow in one, but the price is given two ways on the site and no group rate, capacity or notice period is published. Ask about all of those in the same email.
programs.evidence: Includes a handle tow ticket, rentals and a 1 hour lesson.

programs.name: Private lesson
programs.description: Private lessons are for ages 7 and up. A half day lesson runs from 9:30am until noon or from 12:30pm until 3:00pm, is 2.5 hours and costs $91, with $50 for each additional guest. A single hour with an instructor is $41, with $24 for each additional guest. Prices do not include tax.
programs.what_children_do: Ski or snowboard with one instructor who sets a plan for the group, either a long morning or afternoon block or a single hour spent learning to ride the lifts.
programs.our_note: Ages 7 and up only, so this will not work for a preschool group. Each extra child in the same lesson is $50 for the half day, which is affordable for a handful of children and expensive for a whole class. Ask the ski shop by email how many children one instructor will take.
programs.practical_summary: Two fixed start times, 2.5 hours on the snow and a published price, but no maximum number of children per instructor is stated. Everything else about the day, from washrooms to lunch, is not described on the site.
programs.extra_fees_note: Each additional guest in the same lesson is $50 for the half day and $24 for the single hour. The single hour lesson is $41. Prices do not include tax.
programs.evidence: Includes 2.5 hours of lessons for $91 (+ $50 for each additional guest).

programs.name: Wolfpack junior ski and snowboard program
programs.description: The Wolfpack is Mount Cain's junior racing and free skiing program for ages 6 to 14. It runs on Sundays starting the second weekend in January, costs $25 per morning for two hours of lessons and meets at 9:30am. The site says it is not a learn to ski or snowboard program and that participants must be able to ride the T-bar and ski intermediate terrain on their own before joining. Sign up in the ski shop one week in advance. Prices do not include tax.
programs.what_children_do: Join a group of children at the same level and spend two hours of a Sunday morning riding with a coach, on the groomed runs and off them.
programs.our_note: This is a Sunday morning program for children who already ski on their own, not an outing you can book for a class of beginners. Sign up happens in person at the ski shop a week ahead, so someone has to be on the mountain the weekend before. Coaching questions go to the Wolfpack email on the lessons page.
programs.practical_summary: Ages, price, start time and a week's notice are all published, which is more than the rest of the site gives. How many weeks it runs is not stated, and nothing about washrooms, lunch or shelter is described.

Box 1255, Port McNeill, BC V0R 3P0, which is about 77km away from the hill and would put the pin in the wrong place, so it was not recorded as the address

COORDINATES: the site publishes no map embed, no JSON-LD coordinates and no og:latitude. The weather page links to https://www.windy.com/50.229/-126.326?50.180,-126.334,12 which carries two coordinate pairs. 50.229, -126.326 is the forecast point in the link path and is what is recorded here; 50.180, -126.334 is the map view centre in the query string, about 5km south. Worth confirming the pin against the venue before it is trusted
no group or school rate is published anywhere. The tickets page gives only an email contact, bcolbourne@mountcain.com, for group and school bookings
no youngest age is stated for visiting or for a group booking. The only published minimums are ages 7 and up for a private lesson and ages 6 to 14 for the Wolfpack
whether preschool or daycare groups are welcome is not addressed anywhere on the site
no capacity limit is published for a group, a school booking or a private lesson
no lead time is published for a group or school booking. The only notice period on the site is one week for the Wolfpack
washrooms for day visitors are not described. The parking and camping policies refer to outhouses, and the accommodation pages describe washrooms inside the hostels, which are for overnight guests
no indoor lunch space for a group is described. The Cain Cafe is the only indoor food service mentioned and its hours are published, but nothing says a group may eat packed lunches anywhere
no rain, snow or bad weather backup is described, and the site says there are no services provided by Mount Cain during mid week days
bus parking is not mentioned. The site describes a main parking lot with cars parked within four feet of each other and says tow behind trailers are strongly discouraged
how many weeks the Wolfpack runs each season is unknown. Only the start, the second weekend in January, is published

the ticket, rental and lesson prices are not dated anywhere on the site. The most recent completed season named on the site is 2025/2026, which closed in April 2026, so the figures may change before the 2026/2027 season opens in December
the operational schedule page is headed 2025 - 2026 Operational Schedule but lists dates from December 2026 to April 2027, so the heading is stale rather than the schedule
the day pass prices differ for members and non members. The adult figure recorded is the non member day pass of $74; members pay $64 and a single membership is $20
no image on the site carries alt text, and image files were not opened, so the hero image description was written from where the photo sits on the home page rather than from looking at the photo

the vertical drop is published two ways, 430 m on the mountain statistics page and 457 metres on the activities page. Neither affects a group booking, so it is noted here rather than raised as a conflict

category: a ski hill in the alpine is filed as nature_outdoors rather than community_civic, on the grounds that the offering is outdoor and mountain based. Note that the sibling record mount-washington-alpine-resort.json files the same kind of venue as community_civic, so the two ski hills in this catalog disagree and a human should settle which one is right
no telephone number for Mount Cain is published. The only phone numbers on the site belong to off mountain motels and guest houses

values: 9:30 am to 3:30 pm Saturdays and Sundays, and holidays.
conflicts.note: Two of their pages give different days. One says Saturday, Sunday and select Mondays, the other says Saturdays, Sundays and holidays. Mondays are the days school groups get, so settle the date when you book.
The beginner package is priced two ways on their site, $47.25 plus tax on one page and $48 on the other. Ask which one applies when you book.
